context: Builds on Router ID, configured OSPF neighbors and route observations. This exercise supplies one compatible two-way broadcast segment.
goal: Prepare a shared OSPF segment for a later high-priority router and the loss of the first designated router.

concepts.title: Decide who can take a role
concepts.text: On a shared broadcast segment, OSPF chooses a designated router (DR) and a backup (BDR). An interface priority of zero excludes that router from those roles. It can still be an OSPF neighbor. For a fresh election among these supplied routers, the larger priority wins. If priorities tie, compare numerical Router IDs.

concepts.title: Keep an established leader through a later arrival
concepts.text: The priority determines eligibility and helps choose an open role. A router joining this established segment with a higher priority keeps the current DR and BDR in place. Compare a fresh election with a later arrival before planning any interruption.

concepts.title: Observe failover and neighbor choices
concepts.text: If the DR goes down, the eligible BDR takes over and a new backup can be chosen. A pair of compatible routers involving a DR or BDR would attempt full adjacency. Two other routers can stay two-way neighbors. This exercise shows that decision from the settled roles.

worked.explanation: Bridge priority 90 beats Depot 70. Meter has priority 0 and can still be a neighbor.

worked.label: Later arrival
worked.explanation: The earlier DR and BDR remain. A larger number on the newcomer does not move either incumbent.

worked.label: Bridge outage
worked.explanation: The original backup takes over. Meter can attempt adjacency with either elected router.

practice.title: Set the training priorities
practice.action: Enter 110 for Library, 70 for Workshop, and 0 for Desk.
practice.observe: Library and Workshop win on the fresh segment. Desk stays a neighbor without a designated role.

practice.title: Compare a later arrival
practice.observe: Annex is present with a higher priority. Library still serves as DR and Workshop as BDR.

practice.title: Check the named outage
practice.action: Select Library outage. Read the displayed roles and the Desk neighbor comparisons. Select Check workspace.
practice.observe: Workshop takes over. Annex can fill the open backup role, and Desk can attempt adjacency with it.

requirements: On a fresh Research segment, make North the designated router and West the backup. Set their priorities below Relay’s supplied priority.
Keep Observer on the segment without allowing it to become a designated router or backup.
Check that Relay’s later arrival leaves the incumbent roles in place, then verify that West takes over when North goes down.

review.introduction: Explains eligibility, fresh election, non-preempting arrival and backup promotion with a worked segment.
review.example: Learners change three interface priorities and inspect separate derived role and adjacency views.
review.assignment: Independent configuration and useful feedback across fresh election, arrival and outage. The role choices are computed.
